intent_en: To question the policy priority of vaccine boosters in high-income countries given the severe inequality in initial vaccine distribution across global income groups.
previous_intent: To illustrate the vast inequality in vaccine distribution across global income levels and question the policy rationale for prioritizing booster shots when primary vaccination is so unevenly distributed.
narration_support: Considering that so unequally distributed should we be concerned ab a third shot when so many had their first.
chart_support: Horizontal bar chart showing the share of population vaccinated (fully, partially, not vaccinated) and boosters (highlighted in yellow) across different income levels (high, upper-middle, lower-middle, low), illustrating a massive disparity in coverage where high-income nations have significant vaccination and booster rates while low-income nations have minimal coverage.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly questions the third shot (booster) in the context of unequal distribution. The chart visualizes this inequality, showing high vaccination and booster rates (yellow bars) for high-income countries versus near-zero rates for low-income countries.
